candidates.prompt_text: Do you like learning with friends? Please say why or why not.
suggested_ideas: how you feel when studying with friends
one good thing about learning with friends

evaluation_guide.expected_content: A short personal answer about whether the speaker likes learning with friends, with at least one simple reason.
evaluation_guide.key_points: Clear opinion; simple reason such as sharing ideas, feeling happier, or easier practice; understandable pronunciation of common words.
evaluation_guide.acceptable_responses: Yes/no answers are both acceptable. The student may mention studying in class, doing homework together, or practicing speaking with classmates or friends.
evaluation_guide.off_topic_examples: Talking mainly about a favorite school subject without mentioning friends; describing a family member; discussing travel or expensive courses.
evaluation_guide.scoring_hints: Focus on intelligibility, stress, and basic sound production. Reward clear delivery even if grammar is simple. A brief but direct answer can still be successful.
evaluation_guide.common_mistakes: Very quiet speech; unclear final sounds; dropping important words; giving no reason; long pauses that make the message hard to follow.

candidates.prompt_text: Tell me about one activity you do when you learn with friends.

evaluation_guide.expected_content: A simple description of one learning activity the speaker does with friends.
evaluation_guide.key_points: Name one activity; give one or two details about how it happens; speak clearly enough for an average listener to understand.
evaluation_guide.acceptable_responses: Any common learning activity is acceptable, such as discussing lessons, practicing English, solving exercises together, or explaining ideas to each other.
evaluation_guide.off_topic_examples: Describing a sports game with friends only; listing many school rules; talking about a teacher instead of a shared activity.
evaluation_guide.scoring_hints: Listen for clear consonants and vowels in familiar words, natural word stress, and overall intelligibility. Minor grammar errors should not reduce the score if pronunciation is clear.
evaluation_guide.common_mistakes: Speaking too fast and swallowing sounds; repeating the same word many times without adding detail; answering with only one word; unclear sentence endings.

candidates.prompt_text: Describe a time when studying with friends helped you learn better.

evaluation_guide.expected_content: A brief past example of learning with friends and a simple explanation of how it was helpful.
evaluation_guide.key_points: Mention a specific study situation; describe one helpful action from friends; explain the result, such as better understanding or more confidence.
evaluation_guide.acceptable_responses: The student may talk about group study at school, preparing for a test, practicing a lesson, or reviewing homework together. Exact details may be simple.
evaluation_guide.off_topic_examples: Talking only about playing with friends; discussing family study habits; giving general opinions with no example at all.
evaluation_guide.scoring_hints: Prioritize understandable pronunciation across short connected speech. Notice whether key words are clear and whether pausing supports meaning. Do not over-penalize simple tense errors.
evaluation_guide.common_mistakes: No clear example; hard-to-hear key words; monotone delivery that hides meaning; long hesitation before basic words; ending before explaining how the friends helped.
